questions.question: Two resistors, one of 12 Ω and the other of 24 Ω are connected in parallel. This combination is connected in series with a 22 Ω resistor and a 12 V battery. The current in the 12 Ω resistor is __________.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer-Option 4- **(4/15) A**

__
 
• The two resistors one of 12 Ω and the other of 24 Ω are in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2
 
• 1/R = 1/12 + 1/24
 
• 1/R = 1/8
 
• Equivalent resistance of these two resistors = 8 Ω
 
• Now this resistance is connected in series with 22 Ω resistor. The equivalent resistance will be the sum = 22 Ω + 8 Ω = 30 Ω
 
• Voltage = Current X Resistance
 
• Current flowing in the circuit= 12/30 Ampere
 
• But, we need to find current in the 12 Ω resistor.
 
• Please note that when two resistors are connected in parallel, the voltage drop across each resistors is the same but the current is not. When resistors are connected in series, the current flowing is the same but the voltage drop across each resistors would be different. 
 
• Hence, the current flowing through 8 Ω (equivalent resistance of 12 Ω and 24 Ω) is 12/30 Ampere and the voltage drop across it is 8 X 12/30= 3.2 Volts.
 
• To find the current flowing in the 12 Ω resistor, Voltage= 3.2 Volts.
 
• I = 3.2/12 = **4/15 Ampere**__.

questions.question: What type of Flip Flop is used in Counters?
questions.solution:
A T flip-flop, also known as a toggle flip-flop, has a single input called T (toggle) and a single output Q. When the T input is high (logic 1) and the flip-flop is triggered by a clock pulse, the output toggles between its previous state and its complemented state.

In other words, if the output was 0 before the , it becomes 1 after the pulse; if it was 1, it becomes 0.

By using T flip-flops in a counter, we can create a circuit that counts by toggling the output of each flip-flop on each clock pulse.

For example, in a 2-bit counter, we can use two T flip-flops connected in a chain, with the output of the first flip-flop connected to the input of the second flip-flop, and the clock input of both flip-flops connected to the same clock signal.

The output of the first flip-flop toggles on each clock pulse, and the output of the second flip-flop toggles on each second clock pulse, creating a 2-bit binary count.

questions.question: Race Around condition can be avoided in Digital logic circuits using _______.
questions.solution:

Race around can be avoided by using a Master-Slave Flip-flop as shown:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/09f0c89277a61853abfa78683748005726a63e56fbd78a98f9bf289a1b287823.png] 

Working of Master-Slave flip flop

1) When CLK = High, the Master will be active and the slave will be inactive.

Feedback values don’t change as slave flip flop is inactive. Due to this Master output Toggles only once in one clock pulse.

2) When CLK = low, the latest master outputs are transferred to slave inputs and output is obtained. That is slave output change only once in one clock pulse.

3) Master-Slave JK flip flop is similar to the negative edge triggered flip flop

4) Master-Slave JK flip flop also can be converted to positive edge-triggered as shown

Race around condition (RAC)

Race around condition occurs only in level-triggered flip flop. In this, even though input is constant, output continuously toggles and changes for some time continuously.

This is explained as shown:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dee72ab3b979ca8b39285b5f24be0f1778c012ca7661d32abd3809c9953d703a.png] 

RAC occurs is when J = 1 and K = 1 [flip flop in toggling mode] and tp > tff

Output toggles many times instead of once in one clock pulse. It is undesirable and called as “Race Around Condition”.
